findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "upload_file" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: upload_file · Private data: geocode, question_to_map, reverse_geocode, upload_file · Public sink: upload_file · Destructive: upload_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: upload_file · Private data: geocode, question_to_map, reverse_geocode, upload_file · Public sink: upload_file · Destructive: upload_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool removed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "create_upload" is no longer advertised. Removal can precede a shadowing replacement from another server.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_capabilities" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
